newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond issuance reaches record $678 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond issuance reaches record $678 bln in 1996.

text.p: International bonds worth a total of $678 billion were launched in 1996, up from the record-breaking $465 billion issued the previous year, Capital DATA Bondware figures showed.
The dollar sector remained the top currency with $281 billion issued, a 41 percent market share. In 1995 dollar bonds accounted for 36 percent of all new issues.
Mark-denominated bonds totalled $111 billion equivalent, or 16 percent of the total, making it the second most popular.
The yen came third with 8.2 percent, closely followed by French francs at 8.0 percent and sterling at 7.3 percent.
New currencies tapped in 1996 included the Polish zloty, Egyptian pound, Slovak crown and Croatian kuna.

The sector with the largest increase in volume was the New Zealand dollar, in which 50 new issues totalling over $3.0 billion equivalent were launched compared with four deals for $172 million in 1995.

Merrill Lynch lead managed the most deals, with over $50 billion of bonds under its belt. Morgan Stanley was the second most active bookrunner with $40 billion and SBC Warburg came third with $36 billion.
